problem: The same regime gets two different ranges: the table gives 0.002 to 0.02 for a full film, while Section 4 gives 0.001 to 0.01 for hydrodynamic lubrication. A student revising from both places will not know which range to quote.
fix: Use one range in both places, for example 'about 0.001 to 0.01 under full-film (hydrodynamic) conditions', and add that lightly loaded bearings sit at the top of the band.

problem: 'takes no axial load unless flanges are added' suggests flanges are an optional add-on. In a real bearing the flanges are part of the rings; it is specifically the flanged types, with ribs on both rings, that take a little axial load, and only in one direction.
fix: The plain cylindrical roller bearing carries radial load only. Flanged variants, with ribs on both rings, take a small axial load in one direction.

problem: The question asks for lining materials, but cast iron is normally used as a solid bush, not as a thin lining bonded or cast into a steel shell like babbitt and bronze. The three items are not all of the same kind.
fix: Either word the question as 'materials used for plain bearing bushes and linings', or replace cast iron with another lining material and mention cast iron bushes separately.

problem: The other chapter is named in plain text, so on a phone the reader cannot jump to it, unlike every other cross-reference in the book.
fix: Mark it up as a link to that chapter, for example: Chapter 5.3 shows how the rotating shaft builds that pressure.
